newsitem.title: LEBANON: EIB, Beirut finance house in equity financing fund.
newsitem.headline: EIB, Beirut finance house in equity financing fund.

text.p: Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest (LI) and the European Investment Bank (EIB) set up an $8.8-million equity financing fund for small and medium-sized Lebanese industrial firms, LI said on Tuesday.

Lebanon Invest said in a statement that Lebanese and other Arab shareholders' equity participation in the LI Venture SAL fund closed at $5 million. EIB will provide three million ecus ($3.8 million) under its Global Loan Programme.
"The available funds will provide small and medium size industrial Lebanese enterprises with an attractive source of equity financing which is lacking in Lebanese capital markets," LI added.
The fund will take minority equity participation of between $100,000 to $2 million in joint stock enterprises, Bassam Yammine, LI Senior Officer Corporate Finance, told Reuters.
LI said that any company with a feasible project and good potential for growth and profitability can apply.

"The project has to be environmentally safe, with size that lies within the limits determined by Lebanon Invest, and the project owners must have substantial equity stake in the deal for the duration that Lebanon Invest is engaged in the project," it added.
Lebanese individuals and institutions took up 69 percent of the $5 million equity while individuals and institutions from other Arab states took up the remaining 31 percent, it said.
LI said in March, when it announced the launching of the fund, that it will take seats on the boards of participating companies and give financial advice, marketing assistance and other help.

"Lebanon Invest is providing the beneficiary companies with long-term financing, a positive image, strategic and financing planning advice, in addition to other Lebanon Invest resources," LI said in its statement.
"This fund will assist in strengthening the industrial sector in Lebanon and in creating new jobs," it added.
The Lebanese Industrialists Association had welcomed the fund, saying it and similar projects launched recently in Beirut would give a push to the industrial sector.
